details: CONFIRMED by reading. Project rule (CLAUDE.local.md, Python: "Every new or changed function has types"), repeated in
the brief ("types on new or changed code"). Rated LOW: no behaviour is wrong. Note `dt` is imported inside the
function, so the annotation needs a module-level `import datetime as dt` or a string annotation. Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- plugins/delegate/hooks/route-guard.py: -def running_now(session_id): +def running_now(session_id, now=None):
failing_case: route-guard.py:73 `def running_now(session_id, now=None):` - changed in this commit (new parameter), no annotations.
tests/test_running_agents.py:31 `def load_guard():` - new, no return type. The project rule says every new or
changed function has types; it should read e.g. `def running_now(session_id: str | None, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> int:`.
fix_hint: Annotate running_now (session_id: str | None, now: "dt.datetime | None" = None) -> int, and load_guard() -> types.ModuleType.

details: CONFIRMED by reading the tests and the code path: the current code does put the start in last_seen (it has a ts and
an agent_id), so behaviour is right today; the test set just does not pin it. Fragile, hence LOW. Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: tests/test_running_agents.py:44-47 dead_workflow() adds a tool_post for every started agent; no test has a start alone older than 10 minutes.
failing_case: Change running_agents to record last_seen only for tool events (not agent_start): an agent started 30 min ago that
died before its first tool call is then never in last_seen and is kept by the `not in last_seen` branch, so it
counts forever. All 5 tests still pass, because the dead workflow in the tests always has a tool_post 50 min ago.
The same `not in last_seen` branch keeps forever an agent whose start has an unparseable ts.
pass_cases: 1. Ledger: one agent_start 30 min ago, no other events, no stop: running_now("s", NOW) == 0.
2. Ledger: one agent_start 3 min ago, no other events: running_now == 1.
3. Ledger: agent_start 90 min ago and a tool_pre 4 min ago: running_now == 1 (existing test).
findings.summary: no test that an agent whose only event is an old agent_start is dropped; an implementation that ignored the start's own time would still pass
